solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Former IT boss faces current online stink? Yes, if heartlessly restricted access to posts

indicators.note: one piece faces, or stands in front of, what follows, so it comes first

parts.note: Steve Jobs, the late head of Apple
the Forth is a Scottish river, a current, and E (as in e-mail) means online
BO, body odour, is a stink

indicators.note: heartlessly says the word Yes loses its middle letter

explanation.surface: A gossip column swipe at an old tech chief whose web presence reeks, plus a quip about favouritism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes the middle E of YES to leave YS. 'if' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes posts handed to friends and insiders, so access to those jobs is restricted to a favoured circle.

clue.text: Former poet and playwright can sup Adam's wine

parts.note: can and john are both slang for a toilet
to sup is to drink
Adam's wine (or Adam's ale) is a jokey name for water, the only drink in Eden

explanation.surface: Someone toasting a long-dead writer while drinking plain water from a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: John Drinkwater (1882-1937) was an English poet and dramatist. 'Adam's wine' is an old jocular phrase for water.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinkwater was a Georgian poet and the author of the play Abraham Lincoln, so he fits both halves of the description.

clue.text: Pop music perhaps a bit of a gas, when by Sweet

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece sits beside the other

parts.note: a bubble is a small pocket of gas
gum is a chewy sweet

explanation.surface: A music critic calling some pop rather fun when performed by the glam band Sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet were a 1970s British glam-rock band, which makes 'Sweet' look like a performer rather than a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubblegum is the genre label for catchy, lightweight pop aimed at children and young teenagers.

clue.text: Fool made to look small in outdoor charity event?

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a fete is an outdoor fundraising event with stalls and games
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone humiliated in public at a village fundraiser.
explanation.walkthrough: Feste is the jester in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night. 'made to look' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Feste is the licensed clown, or professional jester, in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Put-down from 15 (piano not grand)

indicators.note: piano not grand means the letter for piano stands where grand's letter was

parts.note: the answer to 15 across, meaning go back
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A snub delivered via an upright rather than a grand piano.
explanation.walkthrough: In REGRESS (15 across) the G becomes a P.
explanation.definitionFit: To put down a revolt or a feeling is to quash or subdue it, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Ring about enclosed cage with more than one layer?

definitions.text: cage with more than one layer?

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a hoop is a ring
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosed, written at the foot of letters

explanation.surface: A bird ringed and shut inside a multi-tiered cage.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'layer': it means a hen that lays eggs, not a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen coop houses several laying birds, so it is a cage for more than one egg producer.

clue.text: See 1
Sitting in Row L, Eton's youngest Member of Parliament?

indicators.note: Sitting in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: The newest MP, an Old Etonian, sitting in a particular row of the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: A group of owls is called a parliament, so a young owl is a junior member of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby owl is the youngest member of a parliament, the collective noun for owls.

clue.text: Cooking ten scones took little time in northern town

indicators.note: in says the short letter goes inside the scrambled letters
cooking means the letters are worked up into something new

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Baking a batch of ten scones went quickly up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' rearranges TEN SCONES TOOK, and 'in' places T among them. Stockton-on-Tees is an industrial town in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockton-on-Tees is a town on the River Tees in County Durham, north-east England.

clue.text: Persistent objections raised then supported, reportedly

indicators.note: then puts the next piece after the first
raised in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: buts are objections, as in no ifs or buts

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: borne means carried or supported

explanation.surface: Complaints were voiced and then got backing: a campaign that would not go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns BUTS into STUB; 'reportedly' turns BORNE into its sound-alike BORN.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubborn person is obstinate and persistent, refusing to give way.

clue.text: Former cricketer, one who philosophised on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: Thomas Hobbes, the 17th-century English philosopher who wrote Leviathan

explanation.surface: A retired sportsman holding forth about life on a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Jack Hobbs was a great English batsman of the early 20th century; cricket is England's summer bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Hobbs, a Surrey and England opening batsman, retired in 1934 after a record-breaking career.

clue.text: Wordplay one clot misconstrued, retaining setter's strict attention to etiquette

parts.note: a pun is a play on words

indicators.note: retaining says the jumbled letters hold the setter's letter within them
misconstrued means the letters are read wrongly, so rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, followed by the word clot as written
the setter refers to themself as I, and setter's is read as setter is

explanation.surface: A crossword setter fussing that a pun was misunderstood by a dimwit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misconstrued' rearranges I (one) and CLOT, and 'retaining' sets the setter's I among them, giving CTILIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctilio is a fine point of behaviour, or exactness in observing formalities and correct conduct.

clue.text: Trusted friend spinning tale before about-turn

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next
spinning means the letters of tale are whirled into a new order

parts.note: RE means about (concerning) and GO means turn, as in your go

explanation.surface: A confidant spins a yarn and then does a sudden U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about-turn' is two pieces in one word: RE (about) and GO (turn).
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego can mean an intimate, trusted friend, a second self, as well as a hidden persona.

clue.text: Printing process Christopher and Jack recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Kit is a short form of Christopher
jack and AB (able seaman) both mean a sailor

explanation.surface: Two men, Christopher and Jack, are summoned back to discuss a print method.
explanation.definitionFit: Batik is a wax-resist dyeing technique from Java used to print patterns on cloth.

clue.text: See 1
Go back through right exit

parts.note: an egress is a way out

explanation.surface: An instruction to retrace one's steps via the correct way out.
explanation.definitionFit: To regress is to return to an earlier, often worse, state; to revert.

clue.text: Prepare for conflict, as doctor crashes into former PM when cycling

indicators.note: crashes into says one piece goes inside the other
cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: Clement Attlee was British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A physician on a bike collides with an ex-premier: a road-rage brawl in the making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cycling' sends the final E of the Labour premier's name round to the front, EATTLE, and 'crashes into' sets the doctor's letters inside, after that E.
explanation.definitionFit: To embattle is to draw up troops in battle array, getting ready for a fight.

clue.text: Condition for face covering finally to be removed

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: finally to be removed says the final letter of the word goes

parts.note: a visor shields the face

explanation.surface: A rule about when masks may come off at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a stipulation or clause attached to an agreement, a condition.

clue.text: Essential to get home by train, leaving behind a second-in- command

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: leaving behind says the next word is dropped from the train

parts.note: taken as the railway train
S is the abbreviation for second, and IC means in command, in charge

explanation.surface: A deputy commander has to get home by rail and is left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving behind a' drops the A from TRAIN. 'second-in-command' is read as S plus IC, not as a deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intrinsic belongs to a thing's basic nature, so it is fundamental or essential.

clue.text: First-rate bishop, one with staff all over South-West Africa once

indicators.note: all over means the whole string is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, read here as AI
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
I is the Roman numeral for one
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: A top-notch bishop with a crozier touring southern Africa in colonial days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like a crozier but is the verb MAN; 'all over' turns AIBIMAN round.
explanation.definitionFit: The country was called South West Africa under South African rule until independence in 1990.

clue.text: Doctor moaned about beginning of bulging belly

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go around another
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered
beginning of picks the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A physician grumbles about the start of a paunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb rearranging MOANED, not a physician; 'about' wraps it round B.
explanation.definitionFit: The abdomen is the stomach region, the belly.

clue.text: Female, going back and forth, put back over-the-top food colouring

indicators.note: going back and forth says the name reads the same either way

parts.note: Anna is a woman's name

indicators.note: put back says the next letters are reversed

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top

explanation.surface: A woman shuttles to and fro, then decides an excessive dye is overdone.
explanation.definitionFit: Annatto is an orange-red dye from achiote seeds, used to colour cheese and butter.

clue.text: A problem afoot with one's rodents

parts.note: gout often strikes the big toe, a problem in the foot
one is I, and one's is read as one is, I + S

explanation.surface: Someone with gout in the foot plus their pet rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' is literal here: gout attacks the joints of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Agoutis are burrowing South American rodents related to guinea pigs.

clue.text: Shipping forecast area of importance when going east?

indicators.note: going says a letter leaves the word

parts.note: weight means importance or influence
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A sea area that matters more once you sail eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC's Shipping Forecast divides British waters into named areas; Wight is the one off the Isle of Wight.
explanation.definitionFit: Wight is one of the named sea areas read out in the BBC radio Shipping Forecast, south of England.

clue.text: Relaying a message, "Is fencing in this sports event?"

indicators.note: fencing in means enclosing, so the run of words holds the answer within

explanation.surface: Passing on a query about whether fencing features in a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' looks like the sport but means enclosing; the answer sits across 'relayinG A MESsage'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Games, such as the Olympic or Commonwealth Games, is a multi-sport competition.

clue.text: Lion Dora shot, according to one saying it's dead

definitions.text: according to one saying it's dead

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A hunter called Dora bagged a lion, and someone confirms it is dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one saying' is the expression 'dead as a doornail'; 'shot' looks like the hunting but rearranges LION DORA.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial simile 'dead as a doornail' makes the nail-studded door fitting the very image of lifelessness.

clue.text: Relative peace at last in French resort

indicators.note: in says that letter goes inside the resort

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A family member finally finds tranquillity on the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece, a sibling's daughter, is a family relation.

clue.text: See 8
One minute after the first Spice Girl gets into Bristol, given this no longer possible?

indicators.note: gets into says the run of letters goes inside another word

parts.note: Bristols is rhyming slang (Bristol City) for breasts, so a Bristol is a tit

indicators.note: after puts the first-named pieces behind the next

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral used for a first monarch, as in Elizabeth I
Mel B and Mel C were both members of the Spice Girls
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pop star arriving in a West Country city a minute late and finding the doors shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first Spice Girl' is read like a numbered monarch, as Mel the First. Bristols is rhyming slang (Bristol City) for breasts, hence a bird's name; the slang is British.
explanation.definitionFit: Once a deadline is passed, the action it governs can no longer be done, which the clue frames as a riddle.

clue.text: Make certain missing recipe is to follow

indicators.note: missing says a letter is lacking from the word

parts.note: to ensure is to make certain
R, from Latin recipe (take), heads prescriptions

explanation.surface: A cook checks the method before realising the instructions are absent.
explanation.walkthrough: R (from Latin 'recipe', take) is the symbol at the top of a prescription.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to happen afterwards or result, so to come next.

clue.text: Act with undue haste, ordering cheeses for nuns

indicators.note: ordering means arranging, so the letters are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone hurriedly placing a cheese order for a convent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' looks like buying but rearranges CHEESES FOR NUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from a horse racing at jumps too fast; it means acting rashly without due thought.
